name: Radio Galaxy Saliency Benchmark
description: This work proposes a saliency-based attribution framework to evaluate and compare 10 state-of-the-art explainability methods for deep learning models in astronomy, focusing on the classification of radio galaxy images. While previous work has primarily emphasized classification accuracy, we prioritize model interpretability. Qualitative assessments reveal that Score-CAM, Grad-CAM, and Grad-CAM++ consistently produce meaningful attribution maps, highlighting the brightest regions of FRI and FRII galaxies in alignment with known astrophysical features. In contrast, other methods often emphasize irrelevant or noisy areas, reducing their effectiveness.
reputation: A very recent, specialized astronomy interpretability benchmark with limited community adoption so far, mainly used to compare saliency methods rather than as a standard leaderboard.
notes: Non-LLM vision interpretability benchmark; small and specialized, with results often reported qualitatively rather than as a single standardized score.
